{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-mo-f","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"da67ba76ee87abb183a2c7325380cd8c224035ab738422b7333e2d55143adcad","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-mo-class-f:lineage:69","source_registry_sha256":"f128002157e581eb7004b9370c8cfbafd7b29a1596262980704fbda0a45932f5","source_liveness_sha256":"fdf72d02e75b9589fee5aaf5b83ec9705ff03586f574464e3553a827f9b698d8"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C2"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C2","chunk_id":"C2.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Inspection and equipment look-alikes: certificate windows, model-year cutoffs, weight thresholds, night-time rules, and the emissions exemptions","heading":"C2 — Confusable pairs and continuation facts: the sixty-day and ninety-day certificates, the equipment model-year cutoffs, sunset versus half hour after sunset, front versus rear plates, the gasoline and diesel emissions cutoffs, and the remaining exemptions","learner_facing":false,"markdown":"## C2 — Confusable pairs and continuation facts: the sixty-day and ninety-day certificates, the equipment model-year cutoffs, sunset versus half hour after sunset, front versus rear plates, the gasoline and diesel emissions cutoffs, and the remaining exemptions
Confusable pairs among the inspection and equipment rules, plus continuation facts that complete part C; each block ties to one guide page, the authorized station sign is a picture on another page and is not described, the emissions phone number and web address are agency contact details and are not taught, and hint metadata sits only in the trailing line of a block.

FACT_ID: sec16-R01 | anchor: A01
A station's certificate is good for 60 days, but a Missouri dealer's certificate is good for 90 days when the inspection was within 60 days before the sale. [A01]
Why it matters: group certificates; confusable station versus dealer certificate; difficulty high.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0085]

FACT_ID: sec16-R02 | anchor: A01
The inspection fee cap is $12 for most vehicles and $10 for a motorcycle. [A01]
Why it matters: group fees; confusable vehicle versus motorcycle fee; difficulty medium.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0085]

FACT_ID: sec16-R03 | anchor: A01
For example, a 2017 model year vehicle that stays under 150,000 miles is exempt from safety inspection through calendar year 2027. [A01]
Why it matters: group exemptions; worked example of the ten-year rule.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0085]

FACT_ID: sec16-R04 | anchor: A01
Vehicles in intrastate commerce registered with the Missouri Department of Transportation and low speed vehicles as defined by statute are also exempt from safety inspection. [A01]
Why it matters: group exemptions; continuation of the exemption list.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0085]

FACT_ID: sec16-R05 | anchor: A01
Any licensed inspection station may perform the safety inspection, and authorized stations display an official sign. [A01]
Why it matters: group stations; difficulty low.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0085]

FACT_ID: sec16-R06 | anchor: A02
Three model-year cutoffs on the equipment list are easy to mix up: safety glass after January 1, 1936, front seat belts after June 30, 1964, and mirrors and pollution controls after 1967. [A02]
Why it matters: group equipment; confusable model-year cutoffs; difficulty high.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0086]

FACT_ID: sec16-R07 | anchor: A02
The pollution control requirement for vehicles made after 1967 does not apply to diesel vehicles. [A02]
Why it matters: group equipment; confusable diesel versus non-diesel; difficulty medium.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0086]

FACT_ID: sec16-R08 | anchor: A02
Commercial vehicle bumper heights are set by gross vehicle weight rating, unlike the fixed limit for passenger vehicles. [A02]
Why it matters: group equipment; confusable passenger versus commercial bumpers; difficulty medium.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0086]

FACT_ID: sec16-R09 | anchor: A02
Beyond the inspection equipment, Missouri law also requires additional equipment such as plates, plate lights and signs. [A02]
Why it matters: group equipment; transition to equipment required by law.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0086]

FACT_ID: sec16-R10 | anchor: A03
The slow moving vehicle sign starts at sunset, while the projection light and towing lights start half an hour after sunset; all three run until half an hour before sunrise. [A03]
Why it matters: group night rules; confusable sunset versus half hour after sunset; difficulty high.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0087]

FACT_ID: sec16-R11 | anchor: A03
Most single plates go on the back, as for trailers and motorcycles, but the single plate of a truck licensed over 12,000 pounds goes on the front. [A03]
Why it matters: group plates; confusable front versus rear; difficulty high.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0087]

FACT_ID: sec16-R12 | anchor: A03
The owner of a truck licensed over 12,000 pounds receives a second plate only by asking for it specifically, and the original plate stays on the front. [A03]
Why it matters: group plates; continuation of truck plates.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0087]

FACT_ID: sec16-R13 | anchor: A04
The emissions cutoffs differ by fuel: gasoline vehicles of 1995 and older and diesel vehicles of 1996 and older are exempt. [A04]
Why it matters: group emissions exemptions; confusable gasoline versus diesel cutoff; difficulty high.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0088]

FACT_ID: sec16-R14 | anchor: A04
Vehicles with a manufacturer's gross vehicle weight rating over 8,500 pounds are exempt from emissions inspection. [A04]
Why it matters: group emissions exemptions; difficulty medium.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0088]

FACT_ID: sec16-R15 | anchor: A04
New vehicles not previously titled are exempt for the four years after their model year if they have fewer than 40,000 miles at the first required biennial inspection. [A04]
Why it matters: group emissions exemptions; difficulty medium.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0088]

FACT_ID: sec16-R16 | anchor: A04
Vehicles driven fewer than 12,000 miles between biennial inspections are exempt from emissions inspection. [A04]
Why it matters: group emissions exemptions; difficulty medium.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0088]

FACT_ID: sec16-R17 | anchor: A04
Vehicles running on fuels other than gasoline, ethanol or diesel are exempt from emissions inspection. [A04]
Why it matters: group emissions exemptions; difficulty low.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0088]

FACT_ID: sec16-R18 | anchor: A04
Vehicles with historic, school bus, shuttle bus, motorcycle, motortricycle or street rod plates are exempt from emissions inspection. [A04]
Why it matters: group emissions exemptions; difficulty low.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0088]

FACT_ID: sec16-R19 | anchor: A04
Gasoline-powered low speed vehicles are exempt from emissions inspection in Franklin County only. [A04]
Why it matters: group emissions exemptions; difficulty medium.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0088]

FACT_ID: sec16-R20 | anchor: A04
A vehicle registered in the emissions area but based and driven outside it for 24 consecutive months is exempt. [A04]
Why it matters: group emissions exemptions; difficulty medium.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0088]

FACT_ID: sec16-R21 | anchor: A04
New vehicles not previously titled are exempt during the model year and the following year as long as ownership does not change. [A04]
Why it matters: group emissions exemptions; confusable with the six thousand mile sale rule; difficulty medium.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0088]
